claims.claim: Königsberg's seven bridges connect four land regions and Euler calls them A-D and a-g
Euler argues full enumeration is laborious and seeks a more direct feasibility test
A seven-bridge walk requires eight region letters; A occurs 3 and B,C,D occur 2 each, totaling nine
Euler states the sum of incidences is twice the number of bridges and recognizes odd counts come in pairs
Euler invokes Leibniz's geometry of position and treats the bridge problem as an example
A connected finite undirected multigraph has an Eulerian trail if and only if the number of odd-degree vertices is 0 or 2 (ignoring isolates); a closed circuit requires 0
